'''Charlton Athletic Football Club''' is a professional [[association football]] club based in [[Charlton, London|Charlton]], south-east London, England. The team competes in the [[EFL Championship|Championship]], the second tier of [[English football league system|English football]].

Their home ground is [[The Valley (stadium)|The Valley]], where the club has played since 1919. They played at [[The Mount (stadium)|The Mount]] in [[Catford]] during the 1923–24 season. They also played a combined seven years divided between firstly [[Selhurst Park]], and secondly at the former [[Upton Park (stadium)|Upton Park]] (also known as the [[Boleyn Ground]]) between 1985 and 1992, due to both their financial problems and the local council's safety concerns. The club's traditional [[Kit (association football)|kit]] consists of red shirts, white shorts and red socks. Their most commonly used nickname is ''The Addicks''. Charlton shares [[South London derby|local rivalries]] with [[Football in London|South London]] clubs [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]].

The club was founded on 9 June 1905 and turned professional in 1920. They spent one season in the [[Kent Football League (1894–1959)|Kent League]] and one season in the [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], before being invited to join the newly-formed [[Football League Third Division South]] in 1921. They won the division in the 1928–29 season, and again in 1934–35 following relegation in 1933. Charlton was promoted out of the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] in 1935–36, and finished second in the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] the next season. Having been beaten finalists in [[1946 FA Cup final|1946]], they lifted the [[FA Cup]] the [[1947 FA Cup final|following year]] with a 1–0 victory over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]. The departure of [[Jimmy Seed]] in 1956, manager for 23 years, saw the club relegated out of the top-flight the following year. Relegated again in 1972, Charlton was promoted from the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] in 1974–75, and again in 1980–81 following relegation the previous season.

Charlton recovered from [[Administration (British football)|administration]] to secure promotion back to the First Division in 1985–86, and went on to lose in the [[1987 Full Members' Cup final|1987]] final of the [[Full Members' Cup]], though they won the [[1987 Football League Second Division play-off Final|1987 play-off final]] to retain their top-flight status. Having been relegated in 1990, Charlton won the [[1998 Football League First Division play-off Final|1998 play-off final]] to make their debut in the [[Premier League]]. Though they were relegated the next year, manager [[Alan Curbishley]] took them back up as champions in 1999–2000. Charlton spent seven successive years in the Premier League, before suffering two relegations in three years. They topped [[EFL League One|League One]] with 101 points in 2011–12, but were relegated from the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] in 2016. They were promoted again after winning the [[2019 EFL League One play-off final]], but were relegated a [[2019–20 Charlton Athletic F.C. season|year later]] after finishing 22nd. The club eventually returned to the Championship in 2025, via the [[2025 EFL League One play-off final|play-offs]]."}}
